abstract: 3D generation, editing, and completion are typically treated as regenerating the complete 3D asset under task-specific constraints, even when only a local region needs modification. This leads to task isolation, inconsistency in content that should remain unchanged, and dependence on task-specific paired data. We address these issues with a key observation: the three tasks all synthesize a designated region while keeping the rest intact—the full region for generation, the target region for editing, and the missing region for completion. We term this paradigm Selective Modeling and build SeMo3D upon it; it naturally unifies the three tasks, preserves unchanged content by construction, and enables training without paired editing or completion data, since any 3D asset can be partitioned into a selected region and its context. For training, we propose region-selective denoising, which randomly selects regions of varying sizes on standard 3D assets and applies noise and loss only to them, jointly learning all three tasks. For architecture, we propose Omni3DiT, a multi-condition 3D diffusion transformer that distinguishes regions to create from those to retain and fuses image, text, and point guidance for fine-grained control. Experiments across three benchmarks show SeMo3D surpasses state-of-the-art methods on all tasks, delivering multimodal controllability in generation and strong consistency and accuracy in editing and completion. SeMo3D further serves as a unified modeling tool for agents, enabling efficient 3D creation through natural-language interaction. Project page: https://xiaokunsun.github.io/SeMo3D.github.io/.

sections.body: The introduction argues that generation, editing and completion are typically handled by regenerating a complete asset under task-specific constraints. It names three limitations: **task isolation**, with separate models and architectures per task; **region inconsistency**, where unchanged regions are altered; and dependence on paired editing or completion data. As an example, PartFlow curates 100K editing pairs via a seven-stage pipeline. The proposed Selective Modeling approach synthesizes only a designated region and keeps the rest, so the three tasks differ only in which region is selected. The stated contributions are this formulation, region-selective denoising trained on standard 3D datasets, and Omni3DiT, a multi-condition 3D diffusion transformer.
sections.heading: Introduction
sections.headline: Existing 3D generation, editing and completion methods regenerate whole assets, causing task isolation, altered unchanged regions and reliance on paired data.

sections.body: The related work covers three groups. Generation methods include score distillation sampling, multi-view 2D methods and native 3D generators, but most condition on a single modality. Native 3D editing and completion methods are either training-free, which keep source consistency but need slow multi-step pipelines, or training-based, which run fast but rely on large paired datasets, such as 100K pairs in PartFlow and 116K in 3DEditFormer. Unified 3D multimodal models are largely built on vision-language-model architectures, condition on one or two modalities, and their editing support still relies on large-scale paired supervision. The authors position SeMo3D as combining selective synthesis with joint image, text and point conditioning.
sections.heading: Related Work
sections.headline: Editing and completion methods depend on large paired datasets, and no surveyed generator jointly uses image, text and point guidance.

sections.body: Each SeMo3D stage works on structured latent tokens from a three-stage encoding. A partition splits the tokens into a selected set S and a context set C, and the model denoises only S while keeping C clean. Training uses region-selective denoising: noise and loss are applied only to S, and the model receives a binary mask. Each step samples full-region mode or local-region mode with equal probability, where local regions are random 3D boxes on ordinary assets. Omni3DiT extends an image-conditioned diffusion transformer with four additions: learned role embeddings that distinguish S from C, a parallel text cross-attention branch, sparse points concatenated into the token sequence, and compositional condition dropout that often withholds the image. Inference requires image guidance, while text and points are optional. New modules are zero-initialized or additive.
sections.heading: Methodology
sections.headline: The method denoises only selected latent tokens, trains on random regions of standard 3D assets, and conditions on image, text and points.

sections.body: On Toys4K, SeMo3D reports LPIPS 0.079, FID 4.99, DINO 0.926 and CD 0.0118, against 0.111, 5.05, 0.908 and 0.0330 for the Trellis2 row. On Edit3D-Bench, SeMo3D reports CD 0.0088 and PSNR 37.39 for region consistency, and DINO 0.875 and CLIP 0.286 for accuracy. On Omni-Comp, SeMo3D with image and text reaches CD 0.0208 and F-Score 0.468; adding points gives CD 0.0133 and F-Score 0.541. The ablations report that removing role embeddings degrades editing and completion, and that injecting points through cross-attention doubles the generation CD. The text states that these results come without paired editing or completion data.
sections.heading: Experiments
sections.headline: On three benchmarks, SeMo3D ranks first on most metrics for generation, editing and completion against per-task baselines.

sections.body: The conclusion states that SeMo3D casts generation, editing and completion as selective modeling, learns all three from standard 3D assets without task-specific paired data, and accepts image, text and point guidance. Agent integration is presented as an efficient 3D creation workflow. The limitations are stated in the same section. The structured latents inherit the resolution limit of Trellis2, which cannot capture very fine structures such as thin palm fronds. The CLIP text encoder struggles with complex compositional prompts, reducing orange fruits to orange texture rather than generating them as objects. Future work points to higher-fidelity 3D representations and stronger vision-language encoders.
sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.headline: Stated limits are coarse structured latent resolution, which misses thin palm fronds, and a text encoder that struggles with compositional prompts.

sections.body: This statement lists how AI tools were used. Codex was used for language polishing, concision and grammar checking, reviewer-style feedback, code development, organizing experimental results and checking references. GPT-Image generated and edited the reference images for the agentic experiments. GPT-6 Astra with Codex acted as the agent, preparing inputs, determining edit regions, invoking SeMo3D, and generating code for the direct Blender baseline. The authors state that they reviewed all AI-assisted content and take full responsibility for the scientific content, code, experimental results, references and conclusions.

sections.body: The appendix gives training details: the Trellis-500K training split, with assets filtered out when their aesthetic score is below 4.5; point conditions drawn by farthest point sampling, with up to 32 points per sample; and AdamW at a learning rate of 5×10^-5. Inference uses an Euler flow sampler, with 12 steps for generation and 50 steps for the SS stage in editing and completion. Benchmarks are Toys4K with 3,180 objects, Edit3D-Bench with 300 editing cases, and Omni-Comp with 180 partial inputs. Sensitivity tests enlarge edit masks by up to 40%, vary the number of condition points across 16, 32 and 48, and compare three point distributions. The agentic examples cover generation followed by two edits and completion followed by two edits.
sections.heading: Appendix
sections.headline: The appendix covers training details, benchmark and metric definitions, inference settings, agent procedures, mask and point sensitivity tests, and extra results.
